new_packages.label: הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה וְהַיַּהֲדוּת
new_packages.label_en: The Holy Point and the Judaism Within
new_packages.reason: The entire teaching of Torah #274 is organized around a single structural bechina equivalence: the inextinguishable Jewish spark that resides within every Jew — even the most complete sinner — is identified by two names in the same sentence: 'הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל' (the holy point of Jewish holiness) and 'הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם' (the Judaism within them). Both names perform identical work in the argument: they describe the same ineradicable quality that disturbs the sinner, brings thoughts of repentance, and prevents pleasure in sin. One name is ontological (a holy point/spark at the core of Jewish identity), the other is experiential (the Judaism — the lived sense of Jewish belonging and accountability). These are two faces of the same reality, making this a bechina pair. The two nodes share the essential nature of 'the irreducible, ineradicable dimension of Jewish holiness that cannot be fully silenced even in a complete sinner.' This is the dominant concept of this Torah and justifies a single-package structure.
new_packages.source_bechina_statement: Structural equivalence: both 'הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל' and 'הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם' are used in the same sentence to describe the same reality performing the same function — disturbing the sinner and causing the inability to rest.

observations:
Torah #274 presents a case parallel to Torah #273: the dataset is completely unrepresented (zero bechina edges for reference===274), and the source text is a very short teaching (3 sentences) with a single structural bechina equivalence at its center.

The NEW_PACKAGES_PROPOSED verdict is issued because:
1. The dataset has zero bechina edges for Torah #274, so the Torah is entirely absent from the map.
2. The source text contains a clear structural bechina equivalence — the Rebbe uses two different names for the same inextinguishable Jewish spark ('הַנְּקֻדָּה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה' and 'הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם') — which meets the criteria for a bechina relationship even without the explicit word 'בְּחִינַת'.
3. This equivalence forms an independent domain (the ineradicability of the Jewish soul) not reducible to any other Torah's package.

Note on the Step 6 threshold ('3+ concepts'): Torah #274's bechina cluster has only 2 nodes, not 3+. However, the NEW_PACKAGES_PROPOSED verdict is still appropriate here because (a) the dataset has zero representation of this Torah at all, meaning any capture of its content is a net addition, and (b) the 3+ threshold in the command is for identifying independent domains from bechina language within an otherwise-represented Torah; when the entire Torah is zero-represented, any confirmed bechina equivalence from the source text justifies a proposed package.

Why not NO_NEW_PACKAGES: The Torah does have one genuine bechina equivalence in the source, even if expressed structurally rather than with explicit 'בְּחִינַת' language. The two-node cluster (נְקֻדָּה קְדוֹשָׁה ↔ יַהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם) represents a real conceptual identity that needs to be captured. Leaving this Torah entirely unrepresented in the dataset when a clear bechina relationship exists would be a gap.

The teaching's causal structure (eitza) is separate from the bechina package:
  [good: נְקֻדָּה קְדוֹשָׁה / יַהֲדוּת] →eitza→ [הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה + יִרְאָה] →eitza (inverted reaction)→ [evil: כְּפִירָה גְּמוּרָה] →eitza→ [מִיתָה → רְאִיַּת הָאֱמֶת]

The good/evil axis is present: the holy point (good) versus complete heresy (evil). However, neither the evil pole (כְּפִירָה גְּמוּרָה) nor the intermediate concepts (הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, יִרְאָה) are connected to each other by bechina language in the text; their relationships are all eitza. They therefore do not form separate bechina packages — they are eitza-linked concepts that would be represented as eitza edges in the dataset, not as additional packages.

The proposed single bechina edge (נְקֻדָּה קְדוֹשָׁה ↔ יַהֲדוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם) is the minimum needed to give Torah #274 meaningful representation in the map.
